content.title: About
content.content: Honeydew melon (Cucumis melo var. inodorus) is a sweet, juicy fruit of the cucurbit family. It has a smooth light‑green rind and bright orange‑yellow flesh, rich in water, vitamins, and minerals. Consumed fresh, it is also used in salads, smoothies, and desserts.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name “honeydew” comes from its honey‑like sweetness.
Unlike most melons, it has little to no aromatic scent.
In ancient Rome, honeydew was prized as a refreshing summer fruit.
Its flesh is about 90 % water, making it an excellent hydrating snack.
In Japan, thin slices are sometimes served with a dash of soy sauce.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains vitamin A and beta‑carotene
items.content: These nutrients help maintain healthy vision and skin.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: One cup of diced honeydew provides about 60 kcal, making it diet‑friendly.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and supports heart function.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes regular digestion and a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to cucurbit fruits.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: People with diabetes should monitor portion size due to the fruit’s natural sugars.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Improper storage can lead to bacterial growth and food poisoning.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Honeydew is eaten fresh, cut into cubes or wedges. It can be added to fruit salads, smoothies, yogurts, cold soups, and desserts. Before eating, rinse the rind and remove the seeds.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the melon in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C in the fruit drawer. Whole melons keep fresh for up to 1 week; cut pieces last 3‑4 days in an airtight container. Do not keep at room temperature for more than 2 days, as texture and flavor deteriorate quickly.
